## The question

[hiding TikZ definitions inside a namespace](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/732258/hiding-tikz-definitions-inside-a-namespace), asked by [N. Virgo](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/12461/n-virgo) on TeX Stack Exchange (2024-12-05; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> I'm writing a package that I hope to eventually release, which will contain a lot of tikz macros. It will contain a few styles with short names like `box`, and I'm hoping that I can hide those inside the `pgfkeys` hierarchy so as not to pollute the global namespace.
>
> What I'm imagining is that there might be a key `/my package/box`, and the user can use it with something along the lines of
> ```latex
> \begin{tikzpicture}[my package]
>    \node[box] at (0,0);
> \end{tikzpicture}
> ```
>
> However, I can't seem to work out how to do such a simple thing. Here is an MWE for one of my attempts, but it fails with `I do not know the key '/tikz/box'`, so it's evidently not looking inside the `/tikz/my package` namespace.
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \usepackage{tikz}
>
> \tikzset{
> 	my package/.style = {}, % without this it complains about the key /tikz/my package not existing
> 	my package/box/.style = {
> 		rounded corners=1mm
> 	}
> }
>
> \begin{document}
>
> \begin{tikzpicture}[my package]
>    \node[box] at (0,0);
> \end{tikzpicture}
>
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> I'm not attached to the package being used in exactly this way - the code above is just an example. What I'm looking for is the "right way" to make my package easy to use while avoiding potential name clashes.
:::

Based on your MWE, you want the `[mypackage]` key to install styles into the current scope. I do that with a style that adds styles. For instance:

```latex
\documentclass{standalone}
\usepackage{tikz}

\tikzset{
    my package/.style = {
        box/.style = {
            draw,
            rounded corners=1mm
        }
}}

\begin{document}

\begin{tikzpicture}[my package]
   \node[box] at (0,0) {box};
\end{tikzpicture}

\end{document}
```

If your example is much, much bigger, there might be some performance hit from installing these styles over and over. In that case, maybe you could use aliases or another solution.
